question: Why is hourly urine output a reliable way to monitor a patient in shock?

options.A: The bladder relaxes completely when blood pressure falls too low
options.B: Fluid intake must match output within a strict ten-minute window
options.C: Kidneys shut down urine production early to save fluid when perfusion drops
options.D: Urine turns dark because red blood cells break down rapidly

explanation: Because the kidneys receive lower priority during shunting, urine production drops quickly when overall perfusion is failing. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h4)

question: How would a patient most likely contract iatrogenic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease?

options.A: Through a contaminated surgical tool
options.B: Through a mosquito bite in a tropical zone
options.C: By inheriting a mutated genetic trait
options.D: By eating undercooked beef products

explanation: You nailed it! 'Iatrogenic' means it happened accidentally during a medical or surgical procedure, such as using instruments that previously touched infected tissue.

question: Why must a scrub nurse know the exact name and purpose of every surgical instrument?

options.A: It is a legal requirement for writing the patient's record
options.B: It helps the doctor finish the operation without speaking
options.C: It prevents prolonged surgery and accidental tissue damage
options.D: It stops the instruments from rusting during the procedure

explanation: Knowing your tools allows you to anticipate the surgeon's needs quickly, keeping the operation safe and efficient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to watch a patient closely after they get IV contrast dye for a scan?

options.A: To watch for delayed allergic reactions and kidney stress
options.B: To measure how fast the dye exits through sweat glands
options.C: To prevent the intravenous site from leaking sterile water
options.D: To ensure the patient does not fall asleep too quickly

explanation: Contrast dye can sometimes trigger sneaky allergic reactions or put extra stress on the kidneys, so post-procedure monitoring is a must.

question: You check an ECG strip and see the spaces between the R waves are all over the place. Which step of your review does this fall under?

options.A: P wave morphology
options.B: ST segment elevation
options.C: Rhythm
options.D: PR interval duration

explanation: Checking if those R waves are marching evenly helps you figure out if the heart rhythm is regular or not.

question: What is the primary danger of running out of injection safety commodities at a health clinic?

options.A: Clinicians may resort to reusing single-use equipment.
options.B: Medications will automatically expire much faster.
options.C: The cost of electricity at the facility will increase.
options.D: Patients will completely stop visiting the facility for care.

explanation: When basic injection supplies run out, desperate staff may unfortunately reuse disposable syringes, spreading infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h1)

question: How does a copper IUD mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By releasing high doses of estrogen to stop ovulation
options.B: By swelling the cervix shut so sperm cannot enter
options.C: By physically blocking the Fallopian tubes with wire
options.D: By releasing copper ions that stun and damage sperm cells

explanation: The copper creates an environment that sperm really hate. It damages them and stops them from ever reaching the egg!

question: While helping a patient walk, you notice their urine bag is hanging higher than their bladder. Why is this a problem?

options.A: Urine can flow backward into the bladder and cause an infection
options.B: The urine output will instantly turn bright red with blood
options.C: The plastic collection tubing will melt from body heat
options.D: The catheter balloon will automatically pop from the extra pressure

explanation: Gravity works both ways! If the bag is higher than the bladder, contaminated urine can flow right back inside and give the patient a nasty urinary tract infection.

question: Which of these is a classic example of an independent nursing intervention?

options.A: Ordering a diagnostic blood panel for a newly admitted patient
options.B: Setting up a surgical tray for a bedside chest tube insertion
options.C: Repositioning a bedbound patient every two hours to prevent pressure sores
options.D: Administering a prescribed dose of intravenous antibiotic medication

explanation: As a nurse, you don't need a doctor's order to turn a patient to protect their skin! That is something you can assess and do independently.

question: What is the main purpose of denial when a patient first receives a terminal diagnosis?

options.A: It acts as a protective shield against shocking news
options.B: It stops the physical progression of organ failure
options.C: It proves the patient is uncooperative with staff
options.D: It permanently cures the underlying medical disease

explanation: Denial is a normal psychological buffer that gives the human mind time to slowly accept overwhelming reality. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h2)

question: What is the main difference between atrial fibrillation and a normal sinus rhythm?

options.A: The electrical signal travels backward from the purkinje fibers
options.B: The upper chambers quiver chaotically instead of contracting effectively
options.C: The heart rate drops permanently below forty beats per minute
options.D: The lower chambers stop receiving blood from the lungs entirely

explanation: In atrial fibrillation (A-fib), the upper chambers (atria) don't squeeze neatly—they kind of jitter or quiver instead. Think of it as a shaky handshake instead of a firm pump!

question: Which sign is a classic clue that someone has hyperthyroidism?

options.A: SlOWed heart rate and sluggish mentation
options.B: Intolerance to cold room temperatures
options.C: Severe constipation and dry coarse skin
options.D: Weight loss despite an increased appetite

explanation: Hyperthyroidism puts the body's engine into overdrive! Patients burn through calories so fast that they lose weight even though they are eating way more food than usual.

question: Which condition is characterized by inherited deficiencies in specific clotting factors?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Deep vein thrombosis
options.C: Hemophilia
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Hemophilia is a well-known genetic disorder where the body lacks certain clotting factors, leading to prolonged bleeding episodes. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why might a nurse need to drain a huge, overfilled bladder in stages instead of all at once?

options.A: To ensure the drainage bag does not overflow onto the floor
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling a sudden surge of happiness
options.C: To give the laboratory technicians enough time to test the urine
options.D: To prevent rapid decompression injury and bleeding inside the bladder

explanation: Draining a massive amount of urine too fast can cause the blood vessels inside the bladder wall to burst and bleed. Slow and steady is safer here!

question: How does a nurse's role in a primary health center usually differ from working in a big teaching hospital?

options.A: Primary nurses work with greater independence in community wellness and prevention
options.B: Tertiary nurses never administer medications or check vital signs
options.C: Primary nurses only perform complex open-heart surgeries daily
options.D: Tertiary nurses do not require any formal nursing education

explanation: At a primary health center, nurses often run clinics independently, focusing heavily on health promotion, immunizations, and spotting community health issues early.

question: Besides the risk of physical infection, what immediate emotional impact does a needle-stick injury often have on a nurse?

options.A: Complete temporary paralysis of the affected hand
options.B: Immediate dismissal from their nursing position
options.C: Automatic immunity to all future bloodborne viruses
options.D: Severe psychological stress and anxiety while waiting for test results

explanation: So true. Waiting for screening results after a needle poke can cause a lot of worry and sleepless nights. That's why prevention is always your best friend! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: Taking daily preventive antibiotics
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Spraying rooms with strong disinfectants
options.D: Wearing sterile gloves at all times

explanation: Simple soap and water (or alcohol rub) save lives! Good hand hygiene washes away hitchhiking germs before they ever reach a patient.

question: Which imaging test is the gold standard for catching a bone infection early?

options.A: Routine superficial ultrasound
options.B: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
options.C: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
options.D: Standard plain radiography (X-ray)

explanation: X-rays take a while to show bone changes, but an MRI can spot early bone marrow changes and swelling super fast!

question: What is the most immediate danger when a patient receives an incompatible blood transfusion?

options.A: Rapid growth of abnormal white blood cells in the bone marrow
options.B: Complete permanent loss of natural immunity to infections
options.C: Sudden permanent paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Destruction of red blood cells leading to kidney damage

explanation: Incompatible transfusions cause red blood cells to burst, releasing free hemoglobin that clogs and damages the kidneys. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the main difference between clinical fatigue and normal tiredness?

options.A: Clinical fatigue only affects muscle tissue, never the brain.
options.B: Normal tiredness lasts for several weeks without interruption.
options.C: Normal tiredness is caused exclusively by electrolyte imbalances.
options.D: Clinical fatigue does not improve with ordinary rest.

explanation: Great job! Think of it this way: normal tiredness goes away after a good night's sleep. Clinical fatigue hangs around even when you've rested well, making everyday tasks feel like a heavy mountain to climb.

question: Which test gives doctors the final, definitive proof of a bone cancer diagnosis?

options.A: Plain X-ray
options.B: Tissue biopsy
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Bone density scan

explanation: X-rays and scans give great clues, but looking at an actual tissue sample under a microscope (biopsy) is the gold standard for confirmation.

question: A young couple visits the clinic and mentions that multiple relatives on both sides died young from the same rare heart condition. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Prescribe blood pressure medication for both partners
options.B: Construct a pedigree chart and refer them for genetic assessment
options.C: Advise them to change their cooking oil immediately
options.D: Tell them not to worry because heart disease is completely normal

explanation: A pattern of early-onset disease in multiple relatives is a major red flag requiring formal genetic risk evaluation. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Clinical Decision Support (CDS) alerts inside an EMR?

options.A: To schedule cleaning staff for patient rooms after discharge
options.B: To warn staff about drug allergies and dangerous interactions
options.C: To lock the computer screen if a nurse steps away too long
options.D: To calculate monthly hospital electricity and water bills

explanation: Think of CDS tools as a friendly safety net. They pop up to give you a heads-up if a prescribed drug clashes with a patient's known allergies.

question: Why is the brain hit the hardest when someone experiences asphyxia?

options.A: It has a high metabolic rate and constant oxygen demand
options.B: It produces its own oxygen through cellular division
options.C: It stores large reserves of backup oxygen
options.D: It is protected by cerebrospinal fluid that blocks toxins

explanation: The brain is a busy organ that constantly demands oxygen. When that supply cuts off, brain cells start struggling almost immediately. Great job reviewing this!

question: How does holistic care differ from traditional medical care that only looks at the disease?

options.A: It focuses only on spiritual counseling during illness
options.B: It integrates physical treatments with emotional and social support
options.C: It completely replaces modern medicine with herbal remedies
options.D: It ignores laboratory results in favor of patient feelings

explanation: Great job! Holistic care doesn't throw out medicine; it simply combines standard medical treatments with a broad view of everything our patients need.

question: A mother calls because her 2-day-old baby is super sleepy and won't feed at all. What should you suspect as a nurse?

options.A: A mild milk allergy needing a brand change
options.B: Normal newborn behavior that will fix itself
options.C: A serious hidden problem needing urgent medical review
options.D: Just normal tiredness from growing

explanation: Lethargy and refusing to feed are major warning signs in babies. It could point to infection, low blood sugar, or dehydration—always treat it as urgent!

question: What important task must a nurse do right after a surgical uterine evacuation?

options.A: Perform a pelvic exam without gloves
options.B: Discharge the patient home right away
options.C: Administer general anesthesia
options.D: Inspect the removed tissue to confirm everything came out

explanation: Always check the evacuated tissue! It guarantees no tissue was left behind, keeping the patient safe from infection.

question: What does a molding score of +++ mean when you do a vaginal examination during labour?

options.A: Normal, loose separation of the baby's cranial bones
options.B: Premature fusion of the skull bones occurring years before birth
options.C: Total absence of the fetal head in the birth canal
options.D: Severe overlapping of fetal skull bones that cannot be separated

explanation: When you see +++, it means the baby's skull bones are overlapping tightly and can't be pushed apart. This is a red flag that the baby might be having a hard time passing through the pelvis.

question: What causes compartment syndrome in a patient wearing a rigid cast?

options.A: Bacterial infection develops under the padding and destroys the muscle tissue
options.B: The chemical powder used in the plaster seeps into the bloodstream and causes clotting
options.C: Swelling trapped inside a non-expanding cast puts extreme pressure on blood vessels and nerves
options.D: The patient fails to move their fingers or toes enough, causing poor circulation

explanation: Because a plaster cast can't stretch, any swelling inside builds up high pressure that squeezes the blood vessels and nerves. This is a medical emergency!

question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.B: A legal termination performed in a fully equipped hospital
options.C: A procedure done by unskilled persons or in poor medical environments
options.D: Any abortion that requires the use of surgical instruments

explanation: You've got this! An abortion is unsafe if it's carried out by people without proper training or in places that lack basic medical standards. Keeping patients safe means knowing the difference.

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns
options.B: Using private rooms
options.C: Taking daily antibiotics
options.D: Proper hand hygiene

explanation: Spot on! Simple, regular handwashing is the absolute number one tool we have to keep germs from jumping from patient to patient.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care out in the community?

options.A: Health education, disease prevention, and personal empowerment
options.B: Performing major surgical operations in local community halls
options.C: Managing acute life-threatening trauma without medical backup
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital visiting hours and meal schedules

explanation: Spot on! Community nurses focus on teaching people how to stay healthy and take charge of their own wellness.

question: How do secondary bone tumors differ from primary bone tumors?

options.A: Secondary tumors originate strictly from bone marrow cells
options.B: Secondary tumors are always benign growths that stop growing early
options.C: Secondary tumors only affect the cartilage and never the hard bone
options.D: Secondary tumors spread to the bone from another organ in the body

explanation: Think of secondary tumors as travellers. They started somewhere else like the breast or prostate and hitchhiked to the bones.

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations falls under which level of prevention?

options.A: Quaternary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention stops diseases from occurring in the first place through measures like vaccination and health promotion. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the correct order for examining a patient's bones, joints, and muscles?

options.A: Palpation, inspection, then range of motion
options.B: Range of motion, palpation, then inspection
options.C: Palpation, range of motion, then inspection
options.D: Inspection, palpation, then range of motion

explanation: Always look first (inspect), feel second (palpate), and test movement last. This stops you from causing extra pain before your exam is done!

question: What can happen if you mix certain suspensions with the wrong type of liquid?

options.A: The liquid immediately changes into a bright gas
options.B: The drug becomes twice as potent instantly
options.C: The active drug may precipitate or break down
options.D: The medication turns into a solid plastic block

explanation: Chemical reactions can ruin a drug! Mixing incompatible fluids can cause the medicine to clump up, fall apart, or lose its healing power.

question: Why do our veins need a system of one-way valves?

options.A: To handle high-pressure surges from the heart pumping
options.B: To filter waste products out of red blood cells
options.C: To pump blood directly into the left side of the heart
options.D: To push blood against gravity back toward the heart

explanation: Blood in veins travels under low pressure, especially from your legs climbing back up. One-way valves act like little trapdoors that stop it from slipping backward!

question: What is one of the earliest signs that the brain is not getting enough oxygen during shock?

options.A: Restlessness and anxiety
options.B: Slurred speech patterns
options.C: Sudden memory loss
options.D: Deep unresponsiveness

explanation: The brain is very sensitive to oxygen! Long before blood pressure crashes, a patient will often start acting anxious, restless, or confused simply because their brain cells are thirsty for oxygen.

question: Why is keeping accurate records of swab counts so important for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: It provides legal protection and proves adherence to safety standards
options.B: It replaces the need to count out loud in the theater
options.C: It allows the hospital to buy fewer supplies next year
options.D: It is only required for hospital billing departments

explanation: Good paperwork is your best backup! Clear records show you followed all safety rules and protect you legally.

question: What does a high D-dimer blood test usually tell the healthcare team?

options.A: The body is actively forming and breaking down blood clots
options.B: The patient has a severe primary iron deficiency anemia
options.C: The bone marrow is producing too many immature white cells
options.D: There is a complete lack of red blood cell production

explanation: A D-dimer is essentially microscopic debris left behind when the body dissolves a clot. If it's high, it means clotting and clot-busting are happening somewhere in the body.

question: What is the correct order for checking a patient's tummy during a physical exam?

options.A: Auscultation, inspection, palpation, percussion
options.B: Percussion, palpation, inspection, auscultation
options.C: Palpation, percussion, auscultation, inspection
options.D: Inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation

explanation: You listen (auscultation) before you tap or press! If you touch the tummy first, you might change the natural bowel sounds and get a false reading. You've got this!

question: How do rigid gender norms typically affect men's health-seeking behaviors?

options.A: They force men to openly share all their vulnerabilities with healthcare providers
options.B: They have zero impact on how men interact with the healthcare system
options.C: They may discourage men from seeking help for emotional or physical pain
options.D: They always encourage men to visit the clinic for routine wellness checks

explanation: Traditional masculine norms often promote self-reliance and stoicism, which can prevent men from reporting symptoms or seeking timely medical care. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand that inherited degenerative disorders are progressive?

options.A: It allows nurses to completely cure the disease using specialized medications
options.B: It guarantees that symptoms will appear immediately at birth
options.C: It helps nurses anticipate and plan for the patient's future care needs
options.D: It proves the illness was caused by a recent environmental exposure

explanation: Because these conditions worsen over time, knowing their trajectory helps nurses prepare patients and families for upcoming physical and cognitive changes. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h1)

question: How do our veins manage to push blood all the way back up to the heart against gravity?

options.A: By widening the tiny vessels in the capillary beds
options.B: Using the strong pumping push from the left side of the heart
options.C: Using muscle squeezes and tiny one-way valves inside
options.D: By sucking up fluid from surrounding tissues

explanation: Since blood pressure is low in veins, they need your leg and body muscles to squeeze them, plus built-in one-way valves that stop the blood from sliding backward. Brilliant work!

question: What is the medical term for infective bone disease?

options.A: Osteoarthritis
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Osteomyelitis
options.D: Osteomalacia

explanation: Osteomyelitis is the specific term used to describe an infection and inflammation of the bone and bone marrow. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is the main job of a flight nurse?

options.A: Repairing aircraft engines and systems
options.B: Piloting emergency medical helicopters
options.C: Managing hospital intensive care units
options.D: Providing medical care during aircraft transport

explanation: You've got this! Flight nurses specialize in looking after patients and giving continuous medical care while flying in an aircraft. Simple and vital!

question: What is the recommended period of sexual abstinence before providing a semen sample for analysis?

options.A: Exactly one month
options.B: Twelve to twenty-four hours
options.C: Two to seven days
options.D: One to two full weeks

explanation: A standard abstinence window of two to seven days ensures reliable sperm count and quality measurements. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h6)

question: What is the main action the male partner must take during the withdrawal method?

options.A: Taking an oral herbal tea before sexual activity
options.B: Washing the genital area immediately after intercourse
options.C: Pulling the penis out of the vagina before ejaculation
options.D: Wearing a thin latex sheath throughout intercourse

explanation: Withdrawal is all about timing: the man must remove his penis from the vaginal canal completely before releasing any semen.

question: Why do we use standard universal precautions for every single woman admitted to the labor ward?

options.A: Any patient can carry blood-borne infections even if their screening status is unknown
options.B: It saves time by eliminating the need to check laboratory test results
options.C: Pregnant women never develop secondary bacterial infections during birth
options.D: Government regulations only apply infection control to surgical patients

explanation: We treat all body fluids as infectious because in an emergency, we might not know a patient's status yet. Safety first for everyone!

question: Which specific bone cells are responsible for breaking down or resorbing bone tissue?

options.A: Osteons
options.B: Osteoblasts
options.C: Osteocytes
options.D: Osteoclasts

explanation: Remember: Osteoclasts 'c'rve or 'c'ut bone down! They break down old bone tissue to help with remodeling and keep blood calcium levels balanced.

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care when using the concept of basic human needs?

options.A: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible
options.B: Focusing on the whole person and their essential requirements
options.C: Treating only the diagnosed disease process
options.D: Managing hospital administrative tasks

explanation: Looking at basic human needs helps nurses care for the entire individual rather than just treating a specific illness. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of hygiene care for older school-age children compared to babies?

options.A: Forcing the child to bathe without any adult assistance whatsoever
options.B: Teaching the child how to operate heavy plumbing valves
options.C: Encouraging safe self-care and independence under supervision
options.D: Eliminating the need for soap entirely

explanation: You got it! School-age kids are ready to learn good hygiene habits themselves while we supervise to make sure they stay safe.

question: What information does the 'L' stand for in the SAMPLE history checklist?

options.A: Last oral intake of food or fluids
options.B: Location of the primary injury
options.C: Level of pain reported by the patient
options.D: Length of time the symptoms lasted

explanation: In SAMPLE, L means 'Last meal or drink'. This is super important just in case the patient needs emergency surgery with anesthesia!

question: Which tool is used most often during pregnancy to check for physical birth defects?

options.A: A complete blood count
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Ultrasonography
options.D: An electrocardiogram

explanation: Obstetric ultrasound is safe, painless, and lets doctors peek inside the womb to see how baby is growing!

question: What is a common home hazard that often causes older adults to fall?

options.A: Loose rugs and poor lighting
options.B: Bright overhead fluorescent lights
options.C: Heavy wooden dining chairs
options.D: Painted wooden floorboards

explanation: You got it! Dim hallways and loose carpets are classic traps that easily cause unsteadiness and falls.

question: When pulling a cut interrupted suture out of the skin, which direction should the nurse pull the thread?

options.A: Away from the wound line
options.B: Straight down into the subcutaneous fat
options.C: In a fast circular motion
options.D: Toward the opposite side of the wound

explanation: Pulling the thread away from the incision prevents the exposed, germ-carrying part of the thread from dragging through the delicate healing tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: How do malignant cells often manage to survive even when a healthy immune system is present?

options.A: They absorb all circulating antibodies to block inflammation
options.B: They coat themselves in thick layers of calcium and iron
options.C: They turn into benign tumors to trick white blood cells
options.D: They release chemical signals that suppress immune cell activity

explanation: Well done! Clever cancer cells can send out decoy signals that turn down immune responses, tricking the body's defenses into leaving them alone.

question: What can happen during rectal insertion if you forget to use a lubricant?

options.A: Complete liver enzyme shutdown
options.B: Sudden systemic hypertension
options.C: Mucosal tearing and irritation
options.D: Rapid dehydration of the skin

explanation: Without lubricant, the friction can easily scrape and injure the delicate rectal lining.

question: Why is Crew Resource Management (CRM) so helpful for flight nurses?

options.A: It replaces the need for medical equipment maintenance
options.B: It empowers any crew member to speak up about safety hazards
options.C: It ensures pilots make all medical decisions alone
options.D: It dictates the exact medications nurses can give in flight

explanation: Brilliant! CRM makes sure that titles don't block safety. If a nurse or paramedic spots a hazard, they can speak up immediately without fear.

question: Why do older adults frequently struggle with constipation?

options.A: Overactive muscular contractions in the stomach
options.B: Excessive production of digestive enzymes
options.C: Slower peristalsis and reduced intestinal motility
options.D: Rapid absorption of water in the upper bowel

explanation: Exactly! As the gut ages, its muscle contractions slow down. This gives the body more time to absorb water from waste, leading to hard, difficult stools.

question: What three areas does the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) assess?

options.A: Blood pressure, heart rate, and temperature
options.B: Swallowing reflex, pupil size, and skin color
options.C: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.D: Pain tolerance, mood, and cognitive memory

explanation: The GCS is a quick, reliable way to check a patient's level of consciousness by testing these three clear reactions.

question: What is a helpful technique when a Parkinson's patient suddenly 'freezes' and cannot move their feet while walking?

options.A: Firmly push the patient forward from behind to restart momentum
options.B: Instruct the patient to lean backward to shift their center of gravity
options.C: Tell the patient to close their eyes and try to run quickly
options.D: Ask the patient to step over a visual cue on the floor or count out loud

explanation: Freezing can be scary! Using a visual trick—like stepping over a line on the floor—or counting a steady rhythm gives the brain a new cue to help break the freeze.

question: What stock rotation rule should be followed when storing sterile supplies?

options.A: Last-in, first-out
options.B: Random selection
options.C: First-in, first-out
options.D: Alphabetical order

explanation: Just like in a pharmacy or supermarket, 'First-In, First-Out' (FIFO) means older stock gets used first so nothing sits on the shelf long enough to expire.

question: What is the leading underlying medical condition that weakens bones and causes low-impact fractures?

options.A: Osteoarthritis
options.B: Atherosclerosis
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Osteoporosis

explanation: Osteoporosis reduces bone mass and density, making the skeleton fragile and prone to breaking from minor bumps or normal daily activities. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is the main goal of doing a Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT)?

options.A: To measure the exact lung compliance and resistance parameters
options.B: To evaluate if a patient can tolerate breathing without ventilator support
options.C: To allow the patient to recover from heavy sedative medications
options.D: To clear thick mucus plugs from the lower airways before extubation

explanation: An SBT is like a test drive! We lower the machine's help to see if the patient's lungs and muscles are strong enough to handle breathing all on their own.

question: What type of acid-base imbalance builds up in the body during prolonged oxygen shortage?

options.A: Metabolic alkalosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic acidosis
options.D: Respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Since anaerobic metabolism produces lactic acid, that acid buildup leads straight to metabolic acidosis. Great clinical connection to keep in mind!

question: What is the main sign that a mum is experiencing distress during labour?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.B: A sudden drop in maternal blood pressure
options.C: An increase in fetal heart rate baseline
options.D: Severe physical and emotional exhaustion

explanation: Maternal distress happens when the physical and emotional weight of labour completely overwhelms the mum's coping powers. Spotting this early lets you step in with a comforting touch!

question: How does an open fracture differ from a closed fracture?

options.A: Open fractures have a skin wound communicating with the break
options.B: Closed fractures involve multiple pieces of shattered bone
options.C: Closed fractures always require immediate surgical metal plating
options.D: Open fractures only occur in elderly patients with weak bones

explanation: The defining feature of an open fracture is a break in the skin that exposes the bone directly to the outside air. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of looking at clinical signs in tummy (gastrointestinal) problems?

options.A: To calculate the total hospital bill for the patient
options.B: To replace all lab tests and scans completely
options.C: To guess the exact day the patient will leave the hospital
options.D: To give us clues about how well the gut is working and looking

explanation: Signs and symptoms act like windows into the digestive tract, helping nurses and doctors figure out what is going wrong inside.

question: When is a syringe driver most likely to be used for a patient?

options.A: When the patient refuses all forms of nursing care
options.B: When intravenous access is completely forbidden by law
options.C: When the patient needs rapid blood pressure support
